validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: independently confirmed real and under FERC jurisdiction -- Docket Nos. CP20-68-000/CP20-70-000, application filed 2020-02-28 by Enable Gas Transmission, LLC / Enable Gulf Run Transmission, LLC, certificate order issued 2021-06-01 (175 FERC P 61,183); originally announced 2018-09-24 (BusinessWire + OGJ). This is not a GEM-only entity -- the sheet's own cited source (ET press release) plus FERC, EIA, SEC and trade press all independently corroborate it. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as an interstate natural gas TRANSMISSION pipeline (FERC-certificated Part 157/284 blanket authority), not a gathering or feeder line. DUPLICATE: checked against the batch A2 roster's Gillis-hub cluster (P5416 Gillis Access Main Line, P5417 NG3, P5113 LEAP) -- P1294 has its own unique FERC docket (CP20-70) and a distinct corridor (Red River Parish/Westdale, sourced via Enable's Line CP and the Carthage/Perryville hub, running south to Starks/Golden Pass/Trunkline), unlike the intrastate Momentum Midstream (NG3, Gillis Access) and Enbridge (LEAP) Haynesville-egress lines on separate corridors and dockets. No relabeling or double-count found. Two genuine data-point discrepancies were found and are filed separately below (SegmentCost, Owner1) -- hence 'confirmed (caveat)' rather than a clean confirm.

The sheet's SegmentCost ($500,000,000, no [ref]) does not match any independent source found. EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (every release from 2019 on) and trade press (napipelines.com's FERC-approval article) both state $540 million -- a ~7.4% difference, outside standing rule 7's rounding tolerance. See the SegmentCost fills[] record for the sourced replacement value.

validity.recommendation: Correct Owner1 from 'Enable Gas Transmission LLC' to 'Gulf Run Transmission, LLC' (100%).
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's uncited Owner1 ('Enable Gas Transmission LLC', 100%) names the WRONG entity. FERC's certificate order (Docket CP20-70) makes clear the Gulf Run Pipeline is built, owned and operated by 'Enable Gulf Run Transmission, LLC' (Gulf Run) -- a subsidiary of Enable Midstream in its own right, not the same company as 'Enable Gas Transmission, LLC' (Enable), which separately owns/leases the pre-existing Line CP assets addressed in the SAME docket (CP20-68). Energy Transfer's FY2024 10-K Exhibit 21.1 confirms both remain distinct Delaware LLC subsidiaries today, the pipeline's entity now named 'Gulf Run Transmission, LLC' post-2021-merger. See the Owner fills[] record for the sourced replacement.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=operating confirmed with evidence far newer than the sheet's LastUpdated (2024-08-14). EIA's Aug-2026 release (the most current vintage on disk) still shows Gulf Run as Completed/in-service, unchanged since its 2023-01 release. AOGR's 2025 cover story reports the pipeline's 42-inch Zone 2 segment 'fully subscribed beginning in January 2025' and notes Energy Transfer is evaluating a further capacity expansion -- consistent with active, oversubscribed operation, not idling or abandonment. Energy Transfer's own 'Year in Review: Gulf Run Pipeline' blog post describes an active first year of service (property-tax payments, continued Zone 1/Zone 2 utilization). No FERC abandonment order, BSEE/BOEM record (line is onshore, not applicable), or any dormancy signal was found. No status change warranted.
